117897.name: Chabad of Port Washington
117897.note: Rabbi Shalom Paltiel's Patch profile: 'He moved to Port Washington in 1991 to direct the local Chabad Center at the request of Lubavitcher Rebbe'. Agrees: State Senator Martins wished it 'a happy 20th anniversary' (NY Senate press release, 2011); CrownHeights.info (29 Jan 2008): 'Now, 17 years into Chabad's presence in the area'.

117923.name: Chabad of Northeast Queens
117923.note: The Queens Chronicle/QNS (13 Jan 2011): Rabbi Yossi Blesofsky 'became a full-fledged rabbi in 1990. The following year, he moved to Bayside to establish the Chabad of Northeast Queens in a rental apartment on 204th Street.' Now 26-06 213th Street (the article). Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

earlier.where: a rental apartment on 204th Street, Bayside

117695.name: Village Chabad - Stony Brook
117695.note: Lubavitch.com (2 Dec 2019): 'His parents, Rabbi Chaim and Rivkie Grossbaum, founded Chabad of Stony Brook in 1987 and continue to direct the growing center today.' TBR News Media (June 2019): Village Chabad opened at 360 Nicolls Road on June 23, 2019, having 'outgrown its former location in Lake Grove'. Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

earlier.where: Lake Grove (its former location before the Nicolls Road building)

117983.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Kensington
117983.note: Its own description (Benevity's cause page; the same on its site, Chabad Central Brooklyn): 'Chabad Lubavitch of Kensington established in 1993 a Center and a home for thousands of immigrants from the former Soviet Union, as well as American and Israeli Jews.' Rabbi Moshe Chaim and Doba Levin.

118378.name: Chabad of Southampton Jewish Center
118378.note: New York Magazine (2005, 'The Hasids of Southampton', reproduced): 'At first, the Konikovs rented a few rooms at the Southampton Inn on weekends'; 'When TWA 800 crashed over Long Island in 1996, Konikov led an ecumenical service at Cooper's Beach'; 'In 1999, the Konikovs closed on their historic $432,500, nine-bedroom cottage at 214 Hill Street' (its address today). Medium: 1996 is the earliest dated activity, not a stated start; they moved there full time in 1999.

earlier.where: a few rooms at the Southampton Inn, on weekends

118419.name: Chabad of Oceanside
118419.note: The Long Island Herald (on CrownHeights.info, 14 July 2011): 'The Chabad, which has been in Oceanside since 2000'. The Herald (2020, its Person of the Year): Rabbi Levi and Soshie Gurkov 'founded the Chabad of Oceanside 20 years ago'.

118563.name: Chabad of West Hempstead
118563.note: The Queens Jewish Link: 'When the Chabad of Long Island organization was looking to establish a center in West Hempstead in 2002, the Liebermans stepped up and a minyan gathered in their home.' Rabbi Yossi Lieberman.

118541.name: Chabad of the Rivertowns
118541.note: The Jewish Week (JTA site, 10 April 2018): 'Rabbi Benjy Silverman of the Rivertowns Chabad, who has been in Dobbs Ferry for the past 15 years' (so about 2003). Medium: a count back; its listing is in the first online directory (July 2004), which fits.

118372.name: Chabad at Columbia University
118372.note: Its start is Rabbi Shlomo Kugel's: The Jewish Week (JTA site, 27 March 2018): Kugel first attracted Jewish students 'to a kosher hot dog cart outside the gates of Columbia University in 1984'. Chabad at Columbia's own history (Issuu): Kugel, sent to Manhattan in the 1980s, started the Columbia program before turning to Chabad of the West Side; Rabbi Yonah Blum was hired in 1997 to revive it; today Rabbi Yuda and Naomi Drizin. Medium: the campus work may not have run without a break from 1984.

117891.name: Chabad Lubavitch Upper East Side
117891.note: JNS (2026): the Krasnianskis 'established their first Chabad House in the neighborhood in 1991'; the Jewish Link: they 'arrived to the Upper East Side in the summer of 1991'. Medium: other reports differ: an award article 'moved to the Upper East Side in the fall of 1992', the West Side Spirit 1993, and Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 15 March 2011) marks its 18th anniversary ('In the space of 18 years'), counting to 1993.
